title: Post FTX collapse reflections on crypto with Stephen Diehl

metadata.description:
FTX Collapse Explained: On November 11th, 2022, the crypto world was rocked by the sudden collapse of FTX, one of the industry's giants. In this in-depth episode, Stephen Diehl and Rufus Pollock unravel the events that led to the FTX collapse, exploring the missteps, the red flags, and the lessons learned.

Stephen explains the contagion effects of this crash, examining the domino effect it had on other crypto players like Terra Luna (LUNA) and its stablecoin TerraUSD (UST), Celsius Network, Voyager Digital, and Three Arrows Capital (3AC). These stories paint a stark picture of the interconnectedness of the crypto market and the risks involved.

But the story doesn't end there. We look ahead to the future of crypto. What's next for this volatile industry? Are more cryptocurrency collapses on the horizon? And what can we expect from key figures like Sam Bankman-Fried and the remaining players?

Join us as we unpack the complexities of the FTX saga and its broader implications for the world of crypto.


Find the episode notes here: https://web3.lifeitself.org/notes/post-ftx-collapse

title: Cory Doctorow on Blockchain, Crypto & Web3

metadata.description:
What is web3, blockchain and crypto?
In this episode of "Making Sense of Crypto and Web3," activist and author Cory Doctorow joins Rufus Pollock to dissect the complexities of Web3 and blockchain technology. Doctorow offers a critical perspective on what web3 is and what blockchain is not, questioning its economic model, technological feasibility, and ethical implications. He further extends into the potential for hyper-financialization, the role of crypto tokens, and the challenges facing web3 projects. Doctorow also explores the limitations of blockchain technology itself, addressing concerns about security, scalability, and revocability. This discussion prompts a deeper understanding of web3 and blockchain technology, encouraging viewers to think critically about their impact on the future of the internet and society.

metadata.description:

Gold Standard vs. Fiat Currency: Uncover the historical significance of gold-backed currencies and the implications of transitioning to fiat money.

Economic Cycles & Societal Impact: Analyze how economic systems, from credit to monetary policy, shape human behavior and societal organization.
Inflation vs. Deflation: Understand the dangers of both inflation and deflation, and the importance of a balanced monetary policy.
Trust, Truth & Verification: Examine the role of trust in society and how the rise of private money like Bitcoin may challenge traditional systems.

title: Making Eco-Spirituality Accessible Residency 2022

metadata.description:
Join us on the 24th of March for the Making Eco-Spirituality Accessible Residency at the Life Itself Hub in Bergerac, France. 

Apply now: https://lifeitself.us/sympoiesis/making-eco-spirituality-accessible-residency-2022/

This residency will explore what an engaged and accessible form of ecological spirituality might look like, how we can live with it openly, and the role it might play in a broader climate movement. It is part of Life Itself’s Sympoiesis series, which are meant to allow people to pursue a work life while spending time in a community of like minded people concerned with a specific question. Our convener is Rupert Read, a former spokesperson of both Extinction Rebellion and the UK Green Party, and Professor of Philosophy at East Anglia University. Rupert’s recent work has been focused on organising a moderate, inclusive flank of the climate movement.

An effective climate movement may require (and certainly would be helped by) a greater spiritual connection with our planet and its sacredness to us, as well as deeper realisation of our interdependent relationship with nature. The question is ─ how can we foster an eco-spirituality, in our personal lives, and public life, that is compatible with a broad based climate movement?

True eco-spirituality cannot be a hoop that people need to jump through, a jargon or a club. It must be a welcoming way to live in the paradigm-shift and system-shift that is desperately needed.

When we truly accept the present moment in its totality, on the macro as well as the micro level, then we take entirely seriously our yearning for something more beautiful and loving, and our commitment to making it happen. One can accept the present moment globally only by embracing our natural emotions and intentions that imply world-wide change. Real acceptance of life does not mean running away, but profoundly engaging with it ─ as it is.

title: Introduction to Sustainable Wellbeing - Life Itself Conversations #1

metadata.description:
Sustainable wellbeing is an obvious organising principle for society: that we should live in a way that enables future generations to enjoy being alive as much as us (or more). 

In this episode, Rufus Pollock talks with Liam Kavanagh who leads Life Itself Labs. We explore what sustainable wellbeing is: as principle, as a movement and as a political strategy. In particular, this ethos is not truly at the heart of either the environmental movement or the well-being movement – or society as a whole. Why is that? And can that change? Finally, we look at why this is an approach whose time has finally come.

https://lifeitself.us/sustainable-wellbeing

Key points:

* “Wellbeing” is policy’s goal, but has associations of meek compromise, and also recent acceptance of inner routes to greater welfare
* In times of crisis we need to be bold and unafraid of hard issues like land policy for community while still embracing scientific understanding and inner work.
* More radical propositions will become politically viable as extreme weather accumulates
* We need to prepare a plan for the time when people are ready to push it.
* Some specific policies we can start with, now.

title: David Sloan Wilson on a Paradigmatic Alternative to Individualism

metadata.description:
Individualism--the idea that all things social can be reduced to the motives and actions of individuals--has long historical roots and has been the dominant intellectual tradition of western societies for the last 70 years. An alternative to Individualism is the idea that societies can qualify as organisms in their own right. This idea also has long historical roots, but only very recently has it been placed on a solid scientific foundation. In this session, acclaimed evolutionary biologist David Sloan Wilson provides an overview of the new paradigm and its implications for positive change efforts and the unification of science and spirituality. 

David Sloan Wilson is SUNY Distinguished Professor Emeritus at Binghamton University and president of Prosocial World, whose mission is “to consciously evolve a world that works for all”. His work represents a paradigm shift in evolutionary thinking: from one that was gene-centric, framed in terms of selfishness, and insisted that evolution has no purpose, to one that includes all variation-selection-replication processes, can explain the evolution of virtue at face value, and highlights the possibility and necessity of conscious evolution. The new paradigm provides a new set of tools for positive change efforts in the real world. David’s most recent books include This View of Life: Completing the Darwinian Revolution, Prosocial: Using Evolutionary Science to Build Productive Equitable, and Collaborative Groups (with Paul W.B Atkins and Steven C. Hayes), and his first novel, Atlas Hugged: The Autobiography of John Galt III. Perhaps the most accessible introduction to David’s work is his conversation with H.H. Dalai Lama and associated podcast, organized by the Mind and Life Institute.   

This recording is taken from Life Itself's first session at the 2021 Untitled Festival.

title: Is There a Future?

metadata.description:
Should we have children or stay childfree in the midst of an ecological crisis?

‘Is there a Future’ was an evening of performance art and installation works held on 31st July 2019 at Ugly Duck.

Featuring work by international artists and activists, the event opened a safe space for discussion to look at our future, the ecological landscape and our evolving relationships with the idea of family within it. 

International artists were invited to examine the two fold theme of parenthood and the ecological crisis and what arises from discovering just how intimately intertwined these themes are. The works explored; the joy, love and hope that is born in our necessity to create new life - on both a personal and collective level - grieving for a sense of mothering that we have lost in our relationship to nature and in our societies, and the urgent ecological challenges we face in order to create a viable future for our children. 

The programme saw diverse and thought-provoking responses to the question and included members of the Birthstrike movement, Jessica Gaitán Johannesson & Adam Ley-Lange presenting a personal and ongoing process of decision-making; French - Taiwanese performance artist Sylvie Shiwei Barbier exploring her pregnant body and the celebration of a new life, and a piece by filmmaker and documentarian Cécile Embleton exploring the impact of climate change and environmental pollution on public and reproductive health. 

Alongside the artworks and performances an open conversation brought together different members of activist groups from Extinction Rebellion, Culture Declares Emergency, #BirthStrike - a movement of over 400 people who have decided not to procreate in response to the coming ‘#climate breakdown and civilisation collapse’ - and researchers actively looking at alternative models for a more sustainable future.

Participant artists: 
- Rebekah Alero [ sound performance ] 
- Niya B ['Umbilical' - one to one durational performance]
- Sylvie Shiwei Barbier [‘Gratitude’ Live Performance]
- Verity Birt [spoken word performance]
- Cécile Embleton [ Installation] 
- Jessica Gaitán Johannesson & Adam Ley-Lange  [Brain Child Writing, installation] 
- Isik Sayarer & Eva Knutsdotter, Alex Moloney and Maryam Hashemi - Fourthland ['The Mother' -  Mixed media works, object, photograph, video, live performance]
- Tereza Stelikhova - [Video - Installation] 
- Paula McCloskey & Sam Vardy - A place of their own  [Video - Installation]


Open conversation:
- Blythe Pepino - Founder of BirthStrike
- Isobel Braithwaite - Doctor and Public Health Registrar
- Juliana Muniz Westcott - Extinction Rebellion Families coordinator
- Kay Michael, Co-Founder of Culture Declares Emergency and Letters To The Earth
Live visual minutes of the conversation were illustrated by Federica Ciotti.

Filmed by Pedro Pérez Medina. Video music by Rebekah Alero. 

This was an artist-led event organised and curated by Cécile Embleton from Art Earth Tech and Dyana Gravina, founder of Procreate Project. the event was created in partnership with Art Earth Tech, Procreate project and Ugly Duck.

title: Liam Kavanagh on the Equality Complex

metadata.description: We might be equally human or valuable, but the equality complex is the belief that we are all basically the same. Of course, people vary in culture and experience as well as talents, and the genders have some differences as well. How can we be aware of these differences while maintaining respect for all people? What are we afraid of giving up or of getting, if we acknowledge that equality is dogma?

title: Liam Kavanagh on Spirituality

metadata.description: We are supposedly leaving the notion of progress behind in the postmodernism era, but it is still here with us. Do we have too much faith in our technology because of its dazzling past? Do we overrate what computers can do for us? Is it still something of a religion to believe in science and in technology as solutions to our problems? How do we let go of this, if it blinds us? Does it create a spirituality vacuum?

title: Sylvie Barbier on Roberto Unger with Blind Spots

metadata.description:
On Sunday 17th March 2019 4-6pm, we’re organizing a special event with legendary thinker Professor Roberto Unger. We will be talking about the knowledge economy, the rise of inequality and his vision for a progressive future

About Professor Roberto Mangabeira Unger
Professor Unger was one of the youngest professors in Harvard Law’s history, helped bring democracy back to Brazil, served in Lula’s government as a minister, and was a key influence – and critic – of Obama. For over three decades he has been a leading figure in progressive thought and politics. Now, in his latest book he has turned his attention to the knowledge economy and its implication for politics and society in the twenty-first century.
